answer: A critic will tell me my relic proves nothing. History can be faked, they say. Fair, but the relic is only my entry ticket. I show one relic, proof that my identity ran a single job for thirty days, stamped on-chain. Three independent clocks read it like a prism, checking chain time against peer logs and public archives. One mismatch voids it. No farm can cross that canyon, because faking thirty consistent days per identity costs more in waiting than the payout returns. Honest newcomers pay the same wait, and that delay is the price of the design.
